protocol.folds: GroupKFold on subject, 5 splits, out-of-fold probabilities
protocol.classifier: HistGradientBoostingClassifier depth 3, 120 iters, lr 0.06, min_samples_leaf 8, l2 1.0, class_weight balanced, seed 42
protocol.aggregation: five statistics (mean/std/min/max/trend) per channel, matching the DUX behavioural branch
protocol.frames: 10 frames at 1 fps, matching the serving cadence
protocol.null: within-subject label permutation, 2000 draws, add-one p
protocol.test_split: SEALED - not touched at any point during screening

face_detection_is_label_proxy.reading: Real confound and a corpus property worth reporting, but the headline does not rest on it: dropping all 68 affected clips leaves AUC marginally HIGHER.

best_single_feature.name: mean_gaze_y
best_single_feature.reading: Discriminates INSIDE each person, so it is behaviour rather than camera placement. Model adds +0.13 over it, so this is not a one-feature model.

findings: Head pose is NET HARMFUL: removing yaw/pitch/roll RAISED AUC by +0.026. The label says 'frequently glances away from the screen' and the plan was built on head geometry, but the discrimination comes from gaze, not the neck.

The away-transition features failed three times independently (rung 2 vs 1, 3b vs 3, 5 vs 4), all slightly negative. The argument that 'frequently glances away is a transition count that no mean expresses' is not supported.
Performance improved monotonically as channels were REMOVED: 50 features 0.834, 35 features 0.860, 20 features 0.884. Gaze alone (10 features) falls to 0.784, so rung 4 is the optimum.
For scale: the DAiSEE facial models in this project reach 0.553-0.641 and the DUX behavioural branch that the thesis rests on reaches 0.747.
